title: SteerBox: priority routing with cache-aware capacity steering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a region-aware priority routing component ("SteerBox") that combines latency-anchored routing, geo-pinning hints, and per-region token-bucket capacity signals augmented with KV-cache 'hotness' awareness. SteerBox should: 1) prefer low-latency region candidates; 2) honor geo_pin directives from tenant config; 3) avoid sending traffic to regions where KV-cache hit-rate indicates poor state locality; 4) gracefully degrade using capacity-aware shedding and circuit-breaker escalation when regions approach SLO-backed thresholds.
background: We currently route primarily on latency and simple capacity hints. Multiple incidents have shown poor tail behavior when regional KV cache warms/cold events reduce effective throughput (large scatter in token consumption and latency). Existing steering pieces (geo pinning, hedging) operate independently which causes oscillation under load. This ticket consolidates routing logic into a single component with explicit cache-awareness and token-bucket policies to reduce oscillation and preserve SLOs.
requirements: Must support: 1) per-tenant geo_pin override with soft/hard modes; 2) latency scoring with hysteresis windowing; 3) per-region capacity tokens with decaying refill; 4) KV-cache hotness signal ingestion (redis/metrics API) and penalty weighting in score; 5) circuit-breaker thresholds that trigger shed-to-unthrottled-fallback or canary routing to secondary regions; 6) observability: per-request routing decisions, score breakdown, and token consumption metrics.
design_outline:
- Input signals: latency p50/p95/p99, region token-bucket remaining, KV-cache hit-rate, tenant geo-pin preference, model-compatibility matrix.
- Scoring: compute a composite score = w_lat*lat_score + w_cap*cap_score + w_cache*cache_penalty + w_geo*geo_bonus. We normalize scores to [0,1] and prefer highest.
- Hysteresis: prevent flip-flop by applying a short hold period (500ms-5s depending on route class) after a change.
- Token-bucket: each region exposes an estimated tokens_left metric; SteerBox consumes tokens per routed request and can preemptively shed when projected tokens reach threshold.
- Circuit-breaker: three states (closed, half-open, open). Open triggers either routing to pre-configured fallback model or returning a 503 with structured retry-after and human-friendly error.
- KV-cache awareness: low hit-rate (> flow-specific threshold) applies multiplicative penalty to cap_score to deprioritize region until cache warms or we route a cache-warming sequence.
tradeoffs:
- Complexity vs predictability: unified scoring reduces cross-component oscillation but increases SteerBox surface area and coupling to metrics.
- Conservative shedding keeps SLOs but may increase cost (fallback to more expensive region variants).
- KV-cache penalty may penalize regions that are transiently warmable; mitigated via short-lived 'probe' hedges to warm cache before moving full traffic.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end proto deployed behind feature flag in staging with synthetic multi-region load test
Routing decisions logged with per-request score breakdown (storage retention 7d) and dashboard created
Under controlled KV-cache drop test, 95th percentile latency improves vs baseline by >=10% due to shedding
Circuit-breaker transitions exercised in chaos test and system falls back without violating customer P99 SLO target
Implementation added unit and integration tests for scoring, hysteresis, and token accounting
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring math and token accounting. 2) Integration test: two-region local cluster using latency emulation + synthetic cache-hit driver to validate score shifts and hysteresis. 3) Staging canary: enable for a small tenant slice with telemetry. 4) Chaos runway: simulate region cache cold-start and capacity drain; assert circuit-breaker and shed behaviors. Logs and traces will be correlated with request IDs.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (FF behind flag, internal traffic only) 2 weeks; Phase 2 (canary to 5% external traffic) 1 week; Phase 3 (gradual increase to 50% with monitoring) 2 weeks; Phase 4 (full) contingent on SLO/alerts stability.
- Rollback: flip flag off; circuit-breaker auto-recovery knobs to revert to latency-only steering.
metrics_and_alerts: Primary metrics: per-region tokens_left, routing_score_distribution, routed_qps_by_region, kv_cache_hit_rate_by_region, region_p99_latency_by_model. Alerts: tokens_left < threshold (warning/critical), circuit-breaker open longer than 30s, sudden >20% shift in routing distribution in 1m window, staged canary SLO breach.
implementation_notes:
- Language: Go (routing control plane service).
- Use existing metrics ingestion (Prometheus pushgateway/edge pipeline) for tokens and cache hit-rate.
- Config: tenant routing profile with geo_pin (none/soft/hard), region_weights, fallbacks.
- Add sampling to always log 1% of routing decisions and log all decisions for canary tenants.
- Keep scoring weights tunable via runtime config and experiment flags.
- Ensure deterministic tie-breaker to avoid race conditions under identical scores.
runbook:
- Detect: alert triggers on tokens_left critical.
- Mitigate: flip per-tenant feature flag to force latency-only routing or apply hard geo_pin.
- Remediate: if circuit-breaker open due to cache storms, run cache-warm probes to region until hit-rate > threshold or increase refill temporarily.
- Postmortem: include route decision logs and token accounting traces.
decisions:
- Unified scoring chosen over independent heuristics to avoid oscillation.
- KV-cache signal will be a penalty (not absolute veto) to allow fast probes.
- Circuit-breaker will prefer fallback region over local retry to avoid congestion multiplication.
next_steps: Prototype scoring module and add unit tests
Instrument tokens_left metric in regional schedulers (infra task)
Build staging harness for multi-region synthetic load
Schedule design review with SRE and Product to validate SLO tradeoffs
